chapter.title: Arms and Ammunition; Parts and Accessories Thereof

page.h1: HTS Chapter 93: Arms and Ammunition; Parts and Accessories Thereof — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: What Israel, the EU, Japan & Canada Charge on U.S. Guns and Ammo | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Five of the eight largest buyers charge 0% on U.S. arms and ammunition; Japan charges 5.4–8.4%, the UAE and Saudi Arabia 5%. Rates and import permits by market.
keywords: can you ship ammo from the us to canada
can you ship a gun to canada

intro: Five of the eight largest markets — **Israel, the EU, Australia, South Korea and Canada** — charge **0%** on qualifying U.S. arms and ammunition, the EU since July 1, 2026. **Japan** charges its WTO rates (8.4% on military weapons, pistols and munitions, 5.4–6.3% on sporting guns), and the **UAE** and **Saudi Arabia** the 5% Gulf common tariff. None of them adds an extra duty on U.S. goods today. What decides access is the buyer’s **import permit** — firearms licensing by police or interior ministries, and government control of military goods — so each card names that authority.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

groups.label: Military weapons: artillery, rocket and grenade launchers, military rifles and shotguns, machine guns

markets.name: Israel
markets.rule: U.S.–Israel FTA: 0% on qualifying U.S. goods (Israel MFN 0–12%)

9306.basis: U.S.–Israel FTA; Israel MFN 0–12% for HS 9306.90, 0% for other 9306 lines (WITS/TRAINS 2022)

profile.headline: The largest buyer: $1.93B in 2025 (+21%), almost all of it ammunition and munitions (9306, $1.81B). U.S. goods enter duty-free under the U.S.–Israel FTA when the exporter signs the FTA origin declaration.
profile.mainProducts: Ammunition: cartridges, shotgun shells, air gun pellets and BBs, paintballs, bombs, grenades, missiles and their parts (9306) · Gun parts and accessories: frames, receivers, barrels, stocks and other parts of firearms and air guns (9305)

regulator.name: Firearm Licensing Department, Ministry of National Security
regulator.requirement: A business importing firearms needs a firearms business licence and an import licence for each shipment from this department, plus an import licence from the Ministry of Economy.

assumptions: Rates are what U.S.-origin goods pay in November 2026. MFN rates are the World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) applied rates for 2023 (Israel 2022) at the six-digit level; a range shows the lowest and highest six-digit rate in the heading. Japan’s rates come from Japan Customs’ tariff schedule of April 1, 2026.
Free-trade-agreement rates (U.S.–Israel FTA, AUSFTA, KORUS, CUSMA) apply only to goods that meet the agreement’s rules of origin; the normal rate shows what non-qualifying goods pay.
The EU charges 0% on U.S.-origin Chapter 93 goods from July 1, 2026 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, whose Annex I lists the whole chapter; the normal rate is the EU common customs tariff.
None of these eight markets adds an extra duty on U.S. Chapter 93 goods today. China’s 10% extra tariff on all U.S. goods applies to these goods but China is not one of the markets shown.
A buyer’s own law may exempt defense goods bought by its armed forces or government from customs duty; such exemptions are not shown.
National 8- to 10-digit lines can differ from the six-digit rate shown.
